textbook_info.name: Textbook Title
textbook_info.overview: 1-2 sentence summary of the textbook's scope and approach

institute_details.name: Full Institute Name (e.g., Indian Institute of Technology Madras)
institute_details.description: Brief history, reputation, and character of the institution
institute_details.societal_commitments: Community outreach programs, social responsibility initiatives, rural engagement, sustainability efforts, NSS/NCC activities

department_details.name: Department Name (e.g., Computer Science and Engineering)
department_details.description: Department's focus areas, research strengths, and teaching philosophy
department_details.faculty_strength: Approximate number of faculty and their specializations
department_details.lab_facilities: Key labs relevant to this course (e.g., ML Lab, GPU cluster)

student_clubs.name: Relevant Club Name (e.g., AI Club, Coding Club)
student_clubs.description: Activities, competitions, how it relates to this course

campus_life.library_resources: Description of library, digital access, journal subscriptions relevant to the course
campus_life.study_culture: Typical study patterns — group study, late-night culture, peer tutoring norms

academic_structure.curriculum_standards: Credit system, semester structure, minimum credits per semester
academic_structure.exam_pattern: Evaluation breakdown — mid-sem, end-sem, assignments, quizzes, weightages
academic_structure.grading_system: Grading scale details (e.g., 10-point CGPA with grade letters S/A/B/C/D/E/U)
academic_structure.backlog_policy: How re-examinations and repeat courses work

student_profile.typical_background: Entrance exam context (e.g., JEE Advanced), expected math/programming maturity
student_profile.batch_size: Typical class size for this course
student_profile.common_struggles: Known weak areas students typically arrive with (e.g., weak probability, no Python experience)

industry_and_placement.industry_focus: Key hiring companies for this domain, placement statistics
industry_and_placement.project_expectations: Whether course projects feed into placements/portfolios

module_details.name: Module Title (follows textbook chapter structure)
module_details.description: What this module covers, its role in the overall course, and why it matters

topics.name: Topic 1
topics.description: What this topic covers and key ideas

topics.name: Topic 2
topics.description: What this topic covers and key ideas

topics.name: Topic 3
topics.description: What this topic covers and key ideas

prerequisites.name: Prerequisite concept or module name
prerequisites.description: What specific knowledge is needed and why

threshold_concepts.description: What this concept is — clear, concise explanation
threshold_concepts.why_threshold: Why students find it transformative/troublesome — what changes in their understanding once they grasp it

misconceptions.misconception: The specific wrong belief students commonly hold
misconceptions.why_wrong: Why this belief is incorrect — the key error in reasoning
misconceptions.diagnostic_question: A question designed to surface this misconception
misconceptions.correct_answer: The right answer to the diagnostic question
distractor_answers: Wrong answer that represents this misconception

stuck_points: Observable sign a student is stuck (e.g., 'keeps confusing X with Y')

concept_inventory_questions.question: MCQ question text that probes understanding of the concept
concept_inventory_questions.explanation: Why A is correct and why each distractor is wrong
concept_inventory_questions.targets_misconception: Which misconception this question is designed to detect

concept_inventory_questions.question: Second MCQ probing a different angle of the same concept
concept_inventory_questions.explanation: Explanation of correct answer and distractors

recommended_sequence: Teach Module 1 first to establish foundational vocabulary and framework
Cover Module 2 before Module 3 because Concept A is prerequisite for Concept B
Introduce Module 4 after students have grasped threshold concept X
Module 5 and 6 can be taught in parallel — no dependency between them
End with Module N as it integrates all prior concepts
